name: Treaty with the Wyandot, 1818 (Treaty of St. Mary's)
nations: Wyandot (Wendat) of Brownstown and Maguagua, Michigan, today the Wyandotte Nation
promises: The Wyandot gave up their rights in the Brownstown and Maguagua tracts in Michigan, reserved to them for fifty years by the Act of February 28, 1809 (Article 1).

In exchange the United States would reserve 4,996 acres south of the Huron River for the Wyandot and their descendants, to hold so long as they occupied it, on the terms the 1809 Act gave the Alabama Indians (Article 2).
landTaken: The Brownstown and Maguagua leasehold reservations, Royce Areas 95 and 96, about 5,000 acres together (Article 1; Docket 212, 1976).
compensation: The Huron River reserve, Royce Area 260, given in exchange (Article 2).
today: The Indian Claims Commission held in 1976 that the value of the Wyandot leasehold in Areas 95 and 96 was no more than the value of Area 260 on the same date, agreeing with the government's expert that the 1818 exchange gave the Wyandot full compensation; this is evidence against a breach. Area 260 was ceded by the treaty of March 17, 1842, which the Commission valued separately at $21,000 (Dockets 212 and 213).
